content.text:
A few things before I start building this.

The DVD structure confirms what I'd expect: `VTS_02` (split across 7 VOB parts due to the 1GB DVD limit) is a 4-stream title with stereo AC3, **5.1 AC3**, 5.1 DTS, and a second stereo AC3 (likely commentary) — that's almost certainly the "play the whole album" title. `VTS_03` through `VTS_10` each have a single 5.1 AC3 stream plus subtitles — these look like individual song/promo-video titles.

Before I write anything, three things:

questions.question: This directory (/Users/rod/build/sfa-extractor) isn't a git repo yet. Should I initialize one before I start adding the script?

options.label: Yes, init git (Recommended)
options.description: Initialize a git repo here and commit the script as I build it, per your standard workflow.

options.label: No, skip git
options.description: Just write the files, no version control for this.

questions.question: 'Extract the AC3 5.1 surround mix for the album' — do you want one AC3 file per track/song, or one AC3 file for the whole album as a single continuous mix?

options.label: One file per track (Recommended)
options.description: Use chapter markers from the DVD's IFO to split the 5.1 AC3 stream into individual song files, named/numbered by track.

options.label: Single whole-album file
options.description: One continuous .ac3 file covering the entire VTS_02 title, no splitting.

questions.question: The individual song titles (VTS_03-10) also each carry their own 5.1 AC3 stream (likely promo videos, possibly a different mix/edit than the album title). Should the script also pull those, or only the main album title (VTS_02)?

options.label: Main album title only (Recommended)
options.description: Just extract from VTS_02 (the continuous album playback title) — treat VTS_03-10 as bonus video content, ignore them.

options.label: Extract everything with a 5.1 AC3 stream
options.description: Also pull the 5.1 AC3 audio out of VTS_03-10 as separate files.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the 5.1 surround AC3 mix from a DVD-Video album release.

Uses HandBrakeCLI (which bundles its own DVD chapter/cell navigation) to find
the main "play the album" title and cut it into one AC3 file per chapter.
Track names are optionally sourced from a MusicBrainz release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

MUSICBRAINZ_API = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/{mbid}?fmt=json"
USER_AGENT = "sfa-extractor/0.1 (personal use script)"

REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("HandBrakeCLI", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe")


class ExtractionError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Chapter:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float


@dataclass
class AudioTrack:
    index: int
    codec: str
    channels: int


@dataclass
class Title:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float
    chapters: list[Chapter] = field(default_factory=list)
    audio_tracks: list[AudioTrack] = field(default_factory=list)

    def surround_ac3_track(self) -> AudioTrack | None:
        for track in self.audio_tracks:
            if track.codec == "AC3" and track.channels == 6:
                return track
        return None


def check_tools() -> None:
    missing = [tool for tool in REQUIRED_TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        raise ExtractionError(
            f"Required tool(s) not found on PATH: {', '.join(missing)}. "
            "Install with: brew install handbrake ffmpeg"
        )


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Command failed ({' '.join(cmd)}):\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}")
    return result.stdout + result.stderr


def find_video_ts(dvd_path: Path) -> Path:
    if dvd_path.name.upper() == "VIDEO_TS":
        return dvd_path
    candidate = dvd_path / "VIDEO_TS"
    if candidate.is_dir():
        return candidate
    raise ExtractionError(f"No VIDEO_TS folder found under {dvd_path}")


def parse_hms(text: str) -> float:
    hours, minutes, seconds = text.split(":")
    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + int(seconds)


TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\+ title (\d+):$")
DURATION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ duration: (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
CHAPTERS_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ chapters:$")
CHAPTER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+): duration (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
AUDIO_HEADER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ audio tracks:$")
AUDIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+), \S+ \((\w+), (\d+)\.(\d+) ch")
OTHER_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ \S.*:$")


def parse_scan(scan_output: str) -> list[Title]:
    titles: list[Title] = []
    current: Title | None = None
    section: str | None = None

    for line in scan_output.splitlines():
        if match := TITLE_RE.match(line):
            if current is not None:
                titles.append(current)
            current = Title(int(match.group(1)), 0.0)
            section = None
            continue
        if current is None:
            continue
        if match := DURATION_RE.match(line):
            current.length_seconds = parse_hms(match.group(1))
            continue
        if CHAPTERS_HEADER_RE.match(line):
            section = "chapters"
            continue
        if AUDIO_HEADER_RE.match(line):
            section = "audio"
            continue

            section = "audio"
            continue
        if OTHER_SECTION_RE.match(line) and not line.strip().startswith("+ " + line.strip()[2:].split(",")[0] + ","):
            section = None
        if section == "chapters" and (match := CHAPTER_RE.match(line)):
            current.chapters.append(Chapter(int(match.group(1)), parse_hms(match.group(2))))
            continue
        if section == "audio" and (match := AUDIO_RE.match(line)):
            channels = int(match.group(3)) + int(match.group(4))
            current.audio_tracks.append(AudioTrack(int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), channels))
            continue

    if current is not None:
        titles.append(current)
    return titles


def scan_disc(dvd_path: Path) -> list[Title]:
    output = run(["HandBrakeCLI", "-i", str(dvd_path), "--scan", "-t", "0"])
    titles = parse_scan(output)
    if not titles:
        raise ExtractionError("HandBrakeCLI scan returned no titles")
    return titles


def pick_album_title(titles: list[Title]) -> Title:
    candidates = [t for t in titles if len(t.chapters) > 1 and t.surround_ac3_track() is not None]
    if not candidates:
        raise ExtractionError("No multi-chapter title with a 5.1 AC3 track found")
    return max(candidates, key=lambda t: t.length_seconds)


def fetch_musicbrainz_titles(mbid: str) -> list[str]:
    url = MUSICBRAINZ_API.format(mbid=mbid)
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
        data = json.load(response)
    medium = data["media"][0]
    return [track["title"] for track in medium["tracks"]]


def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r'[/:\\?*"<>|]', "-", name).strip()


def track_filenames(count: int, track_titles: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) == count:
        return [
            f"{i:02d} - {sanitize_filename(title)}.ac3"
            for i, title in enumerate(track_titles, start=1)
        ]
    return [f"track{i:02d}.ac3" for i in range(1, count + 1)]


def extract_chapter(
    dvd_path: Path,
    title: Title,
    audio_track: AudioTrack,
    chapter_number: int,
    out_path: Path,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    run([
        "HandBrakeCLI",
        "-i", str(dvd_path),
        "-t", str(title.number),
        "--chapters", f"{chapter_number}-{chapter_number}",
        "-a", str(audio_track.index),
        "-E", "copy:ac3",
        "-e", "x264",
        "--encoder-preset", "ultrafast",
        "-q", "51",
        "-o", str(tmp_path),
    ])
    run([
        "ffmpeg", "-y", "-v", "error",
        "-i", str(tmp_path),
        "-vn", "-map", "0:a:0", "-c:a", "copy", "-f", "ac3",
        str(out_path),
    ])
    tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def extract_album(
    dvd_path: Path,
    output_dir: Path,
    musicbrainz_release: str | None,
    title_override: int | None,
    confirm: bool,
) -> None:
    check_tools()
    find_video_ts(dvd_path)  # validates the path early

    titles = scan_disc(dvd_path)
    if title_override is not None:
        matches = [t for t in titles if t.number == title_override]
        if not matches:
            raise ExtractionError(f"Title {title_override} not found on disc")
        album_title = matches[0]
    else:
        album_title = pick_album_title(titles)

    audio_track = album_title.surround_ac3_track()
    if audio_track is None:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Title {album_title.number} has no 5.1 AC3 track")

    track_titles = fetch_musicbrainz_titles(musicbrainz_release) if musicbrainz_release else None
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) != len(album_title.chapters):
        print(
            f"Warning: MusicBrainz release has {len(track_titles)} tracks but the DVD "
            f"title has {len(album_title.chapters)} chapters. Falling back to generic naming.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        track_titles = None

    filenames = track_filenames(len(album_title.chapters), track_titles)

    print(f"Title {album_title.number}: {album_title.length_seconds:.0f}s, "
          f"{len(album_title.chapters)} chapters")
    print(f"Audio track {audio_track.index}: {audio_track.codec} {audio_track.channels}ch")
    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
        print(f"  {chapter.number:02d}  {chapter.length_seconds:7.1f}s  -> {filename}")

    if not confirm:
        print("\nDry run only (pass --yes to actually extract). No files written.")
        return

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = output_dir / ".chapter_tmp.mkv"
    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
        out_path = output_dir / filename
        extract_chapter(dvd_path, album_title, audio_track, chapter.number, out_path, tmp_path)
        print(f"Wrote {out_path}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("dvd_path", type=Path, help="Path to a .dvdmedia bundle or VIDEO_TS folder")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir", type=Path, default=None,
        help="Where to write .ac3 files (default: ./output/<dvd folder name>)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--musicbrainz-release", metavar="MBID",
        help="MusicBrainz release ID to source track names from",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--title", type=int, default=None,
        help="Force a specific DVD title number instead of auto-detecting the album title",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--yes", action="store_true",
        help="Actually write files (default is a dry run that just prints the plan)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    output_dir = args.output_dir or Path("output") / args.dvd_path.stem
    try:
        extract_album(args.dvd_path, output_dir, args.musicbrainz_release, args.title, args.yes)
    except ExtractionError as exc:
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from extract_ac3 import (
    parse_hms,
    parse_scan,
    pick_album_title,
    sanitize_filename,
    track_filenames,
)

# Trimmed real HandBrakeCLI `--scan -t 0` output for the Phantom Power DVD:
# title 1 is a short menu/logo clip, title 2 is the full album, title 3 is a
# single-song title with no 5.1 track variety (only used to prove title 2
# still wins on duration).
SCAN_OUTPUT = """
+ title 1:
  + index 1
  + duration: 00:00:25
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:00:25
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 2:
  + index 2
  + duration: 00:52:36
  + size: 720x576, pixel aspect: 64/45, display aspect: 1.78, 25.000 fps
  + autocrop: 0/0/12/174
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:35
    + 2: duration 00:02:58
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
    + 2, English (AC3, 5.1 ch, 448 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 448000bps
    + 3, English (DTS, 5.1 ch, 768 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 768000bps
    + 4, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 3:
  + index 3
  + duration: 00:03:34
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:34
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
"""


def test_parse_hms():
    assert parse_hms("00:52:36") == 3156
    assert parse_hms("00:00:25") == 25


def test_parse_scan_extracts_titles_chapters_and_audio():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    assert [t.number for t in titles] == [1, 2, 3]

    album = titles[1]
    assert album.length_seconds == 3156
    assert [c.length_seconds for c in album.chapters] == [215, 178]
    assert len(album.audio_tracks) == 4
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].codec == "AC3"
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].channels == 6
    assert album.audio_tracks[2].codec == "DTS"


def test_surround_ac3_track_picks_six_channel_ac3_not_dts():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    album = titles[1]
    track = album.surround_ac3_track()
    assert track is not None
    assert track.index == 2
    assert track.codec == "AC3"
    assert track.channels == 6


def test_surround_ac3_track_none_when_absent():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    single_song = titles[2]
    assert single_song.surround_ac3_track() is None


def test_pick_album_title_prefers_longest_multi_chapter_surround_title():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    chosen = pick_album_title(titles)
    assert chosen.number == 2


def test_track_filenames_uses_names_when_count_matches():
    names = track_filenames(2, ["Hello Sunshine", "Liberty Belle"])
    assert names == ["01 - Hello Sunshine.ac3", "02 - Liberty Belle.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_falls_back_when_count_mismatches():
    names = track_filenames(3, ["Only One Track"])
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3", "track03.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_generic_when_no_names_given():
    names = track_filenames(2, None)
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3"]


def test_sanitize_filename_strips_path_hostile_characters():
    assert sanitize_filename("Sex, War & Robots") == "Sex, War & Robots"
    assert sanitize_filename("Father / Father?") == "Father - Father-"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the 5.1 surround AC3 mix from a DVD-Video album release.

Uses HandBrakeCLI (which bundles its own DVD chapter/cell navigation) to find
the main "play the album" title and cut it into one AC3 file per chapter.
Track names are optionally sourced from a MusicBrainz release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

MUSICBRAINZ_API = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/{mbid}?fmt=json"
USER_AGENT = "sfa-extractor/0.1 (personal use script)"

REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("HandBrakeCLI", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe")


class ExtractionError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Chapter:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float


@dataclass
class AudioTrack:
    index: int
    codec: str
    channels: int


@dataclass
class Title:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float
    chapters: list[Chapter] = field(default_factory=list)
    audio_tracks: list[AudioTrack] = field(default_factory=list)

    def surround_ac3_track(self) -> AudioTrack | None:
        for track in self.audio_tracks:
            if track.codec == "AC3" and track.channels == 6:
                return track
        return None


def check_tools() -> None:
    missing = [tool for tool in REQUIRED_TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        raise ExtractionError(
            f"Required tool(s) not found on PATH: {', '.join(missing)}. "
            "Install with: brew install handbrake ffmpeg"
        )


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Command failed ({' '.join(cmd)}):\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}")
    return result.stdout + result.stderr


def find_video_ts(dvd_path: Path) -> Path:
    if dvd_path.name.upper() == "VIDEO_TS":
        return dvd_path
    candidate = dvd_path / "VIDEO_TS"
    if candidate.is_dir():
        return candidate
    raise ExtractionError(f"No VIDEO_TS folder found under {dvd_path}")


def parse_hms(text: str) -> float:
    hours, minutes, seconds = text.split(":")
    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + int(seconds)


TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\+ title (\d+):$")
DURATION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ duration: (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
CHAPTER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+): duration (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
AUDIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+), \S+ \((\w+), (\d+)\.(\d+) ch")


def parse_scan(scan_output: str) -> list[Title]:
    """Parse HandBrakeCLI's `+ title N:` human-readable scan summary.

    Chapter and audio-track lines have distinct, specific shapes ("N: duration
    H:M:S" vs "N, Lang (CODEC, C.C ch, ...)"), so no per-line section-tracking
    is needed beyond attributing each line to the current title block.
    """
    titles: list[Title] = []
    current: Title | None = None

    for line in scan_output.splitlines():
        if match := TITLE_RE.match(line):
            if current is not None:
                titles.append(current)
            current = Title(int(match.group(1)), 0.0)
            continue
        if current is None:
            continue
        if match := DURATION_RE.match(line):
            current.length_seconds = parse_hms(match.group(1))
        elif match := CHAPTER_RE.match(line):
            current.chapters.append(Chapter(int(match.group(1)), parse_hms(match.group(2))))
        elif match := AUDIO_RE.match(line):
            channels = int(match.group(3)) + int(match.group(4))
            current.audio_tracks.append(AudioTrack(int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), channels))

    if current is not None:
        titles.append(current)
    return titles


def scan_disc(dvd_path: Path) -> list[Title]:
    output = run(["HandBrakeCLI", "-i", str(dvd_path), "--scan", "-t", "0"])
    titles = parse_scan(output)
    if not titles:
        raise ExtractionError("HandBrakeCLI scan returned no titles")
    return titles


def pick_album_title(titles: list[Title]) -> Title:
    candidates = [t for t in titles if len(t.chapters) > 1 and t.surround_ac3_track() is not None]
    if not candidates:
        raise ExtractionError("No multi-chapter title with a 5.1 AC3 track found")
    return max(candidates, key=lambda t: t.length_seconds)


def fetch_musicbrainz_titles(mbid: str) -> list[str]:
    url = MUSICBRAINZ_API.format(mbid=mbid)
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
        data = json.load(response)
    medium = data["media"][0]
    return [track["title"] for track in medium["tracks"]]


def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r'[/:\\?*"<>|]', "-", name).strip()


def track_filenames(count: int, track_titles: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) == count:
        return [
            f"{i:02d} - {sanitize_filename(title)}.ac3"
            for i, title in enumerate(track_titles, start=1)
        ]
    return [f"track{i:02d}.ac3" for i in range(1, count + 1)]


def extract_chapter(
    dvd_path: Path,
    title: Title,
    audio_track: AudioTrack,
    chapter_number: int,
    out_path: Path,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    run(
        [
            "HandBrakeCLI",
            "-i",
            str(dvd_path),
            "-t",
            str(title.number),
            "--chapters",
            f"{chapter_number}-{chapter_number}",
            "-a",
            str(audio_track.index),
            "-E",
            "copy:ac3",
            "-e",
            "x264",
            "--encoder-preset",
            "ultrafast",
            "-q",
            "51",
            "-o",
            str(tmp_path),
        ]
    )
    run(
        [
            "ffmpeg",
            "-y",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-i",
            str(tmp_path),
            "-vn",
            "-map",
            "0:a:0",
            "-c:a",
            "copy",
            "-f",
            "ac3",
            str(out_path),
        ]
    )
    tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def extract_album(
    dvd_path: Path,
    output_dir: Path,
    musicbrainz_release: str | None,
    title_override: int | None,
    confirm: bool,
) -> None:
    check_tools()
    find_video_ts(dvd_path)  # validates the path early

    titles = scan_disc(dvd_path)
    if title_override is not None:
        matches = [t for t in titles if t.number == title_override]
        if not matches:
            raise ExtractionError(f"Title {title_override} not found on disc")
        album_title = matches[0]
    else:
        album_title = pick_album_title(titles)

    audio_track = album_title.surround_ac3_track()
    if audio_track is None:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Title {album_title.number} has no 5.1 AC3 track")

    track_titles = fetch_musicbrainz_titles(musicbrainz_release) if musicbrainz_release else None
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) != len(album_title.chapters):
        print(
            f"Warning: MusicBrainz release has {len(track_titles)} tracks but the DVD "
            f"title has {len(album_title.chapters)} chapters. Falling back to generic naming.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        track_titles = None

    filenames = track_filenames(len(album_title.chapters), track_titles)

    print(
        f"Title {album_title.number}: {album_title.length_seconds:.0f}s, "
        f"{len(album_title.chapters)} chapters"
    )
    print(f"Audio track {audio_track.index}: {audio_track.codec} {audio_track.channels}ch")
    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
        print(f"  {chapter.number:02d}  {chapter.length_seconds:7.1f}s  -> {filename}")

    if not confirm:
        print("\nDry run only (pass --yes to actually extract). No files written.")
        return

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = output_dir / ".chapter_tmp.mkv"
    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
        out_path = output_dir / filename
        extract_chapter(dvd_path, album_title, audio_track, chapter.number, out_path, tmp_path)
        print(f"Wrote {out_path}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("dvd_path", type=Path, help="Path to a .dvdmedia bundle or VIDEO_TS folder")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Where to write .ac3 files (default: ./output/<dvd folder name>)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--musicbrainz-release",
        metavar="MBID",

content.text:
Committed. Here's where things stand:

**Built:** `extract_ac3.py` — scans a DVD (`.dvdmedia` bundle or raw `VIDEO_TS` folder) with HandBrakeCLI, auto-picks the longest multi-chapter title carrying a 5.1 AC3 track, and cuts each chapter to a standalone `.ac3` via HandBrakeCLI + a quick ffmpeg pass to strip the throwaway video. Optionally names tracks from a MusicBrainz release ID.

**Verified against the real Phantom Power disc:**
- Auto-detected Title 2 (52:36, 14 chapters, 5.1 AC3 track 2) correctly
- All 14 chapters matched the MusicBrainz tracklist durations to within ~1s
- 9 unit tests pass, ruff clean

**Worth knowing:** naive `ffmpeg concat:` of the VOB parts silently produced a *doubled-length, corrupted* stream on this disc (its cell/PGC structure isn't a simple linear concatenation) — that's why HandBrakeCLI is load-bearing here, not just a convenience. I installed `handbrake` and `ffmpeg` (already had it) via Homebrew; also installed `lsdvd` and `mplayer` during investigation but neither ended up used by the script — happy to `brew uninstall` those two if you'd rather not keep them.

**To run for real:** `uv run extract_ac3.py "<path>" --musicbrainz-release <mbid> --yes` (omit `--yes` for a dry-run plan first, which is the default). For the second album, you'll need its MusicBrainz release ID and path — just say the word when you're ready, or run it yourself.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the 5.1 surround AC3 mix from a DVD-Video album release.

Uses HandBrakeCLI (which bundles its own DVD chapter/cell navigation) to find
the main "play the album" title and cut it into one AC3 file per chapter.
Track names are optionally sourced from a MusicBrainz release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

MUSICBRAINZ_API = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/{mbid}?inc=recordings&fmt=json"
USER_AGENT = "sfa-extractor/0.1 (personal use script)"

REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("HandBrakeCLI", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe")


class ExtractionError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Chapter:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float


@dataclass
class AudioTrack:
    index: int
    codec: str
    channels: int


@dataclass
class Title:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float
    chapters: list[Chapter] = field(default_factory=list)
    audio_tracks: list[AudioTrack] = field(default_factory=list)

    def surround_ac3_track(self) -> AudioTrack | None:
        for track in self.audio_tracks:
            if track.codec == "AC3" and track.channels == 6:
                return track
        return None


def check_tools() -> None:
    missing = [tool for tool in REQUIRED_TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        raise ExtractionError(
            f"Required tool(s) not found on PATH: {', '.join(missing)}. "
            "Install with: brew install handbrake ffmpeg"
        )


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Command failed ({' '.join(cmd)}):\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}")
    return result.stdout + result.stderr


def find_video_ts(dvd_path: Path) -> Path:
    if dvd_path.name.upper() == "VIDEO_TS":
        return dvd_path
    candidate = dvd_path / "VIDEO_TS"
    if candidate.is_dir():
        return candidate
    raise ExtractionError(f"No VIDEO_TS folder found under {dvd_path}")


def parse_hms(text: str) -> float:
    hours, minutes, seconds = text.split(":")
    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + int(seconds)


TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\+ title (\d+):$")
DURATION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ duration: (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
CHAPTER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+): duration (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
AUDIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+), \S+ \((\w+), (\d+)\.(\d+) ch")


def parse_scan(scan_output: str) -> list[Title]:
    """Parse HandBrakeCLI's `+ title N:` human-readable scan summary.

    Chapter and audio-track lines have distinct, specific shapes ("N: duration
    H:M:S" vs "N, Lang (CODEC, C.C ch, ...)"), so no per-line section-tracking
    is needed beyond attributing each line to the current title block.
    """
    titles: list[Title] = []
    current: Title | None = None

    for line in scan_output.splitlines():
        if match := TITLE_RE.match(line):
            if current is not None:
                titles.append(current)
            current = Title(int(match.group(1)), 0.0)
            continue
        if current is None:
            continue
        if match := DURATION_RE.match(line):
            current.length_seconds = parse_hms(match.group(1))
        elif match := CHAPTER_RE.match(line):
            current.chapters.append(Chapter(int(match.group(1)), parse_hms(match.group(2))))
        elif match := AUDIO_RE.match(line):
            channels = int(match.group(3)) + int(match.group(4))
            current.audio_tracks.append(AudioTrack(int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), channels))

    if current is not None:
        titles.append(current)
    return titles


def scan_disc(dvd_path: Path) -> list[Title]:
    output = run(["HandBrakeCLI", "-i", str(dvd_path), "--scan", "-t", "0"])
    titles = parse_scan(output)
    if not titles:
        raise ExtractionError("HandBrakeCLI scan returned no titles")
    return titles


def pick_album_title(titles: list[Title]) -> Title:
    candidates = [t for t in titles if len(t.chapters) > 1 and t.surround_ac3_track() is not None]
    if not candidates:
        raise ExtractionError("No multi-chapter title with a 5.1 AC3 track found")
    return max(candidates, key=lambda t: t.length_seconds)


def fetch_musicbrainz_titles(mbid: str) -> list[str]:
    url = MUSICBRAINZ_API.format(mbid=mbid)
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
        data = json.load(response)
    medium = data["media"][0]
    return [track["title"] for track in medium["tracks"]]


def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r'[/:\\?*"<>|]', "-", name).strip()


def track_filenames(count: int, track_titles: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) == count:
        return [
            f"{i:02d} - {sanitize_filename(title)}.ac3"
            for i, title in enumerate(track_titles, start=1)
        ]
    return [f"track{i:02d}.ac3" for i in range(1, count + 1)]


def extract_chapter(
    dvd_path: Path,
    title: Title,
    audio_track: AudioTrack,
    chapter_number: int,
    out_path: Path,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    run(
        [
            "HandBrakeCLI",
            "-i",
            str(dvd_path),
            "-t",
            str(title.number),
            "--chapters",
            f"{chapter_number}-{chapter_number}",
            "-a",
            str(audio_track.index),
            "-E",
            "copy:ac3",
            "-e",
            "x264",
            "--encoder-preset",
            "ultrafast",
            "-q",
            "51",
            "-o",
            str(tmp_path),
        ]
    )
    run(
        [
            "ffmpeg",
            "-y",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-i",
            str(tmp_path),
            "-vn",
            "-map",
            "0:a:0",
            "-c:a",
            "copy",
            "-f",
            "ac3",
            str(out_path),
        ]
    )

from extract_ac3 import (
    parse_hms,
    parse_scan,
    pick_album_title,
    sanitize_filename,
    track_filenames,
)

# Trimmed real HandBrakeCLI `--scan -t 0` output for the Phantom Power DVD:
# title 1 is a short menu/logo clip, title 2 is the full album, title 3 is a

# still wins on duration).
SCAN_OUTPUT = """
+ title 1:
  + index 1
  + duration: 00:00:25
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:00:25
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 2:
  + index 2
  + duration: 00:52:36
  + size: 720x576, pixel aspect: 64/45, display aspect: 1.78, 25.000 fps
  + autocrop: 0/0/12/174
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:35
    + 2: duration 00:02:58
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
    + 2, English (AC3, 5.1 ch, 448 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 448000bps
    + 3, English (DTS, 5.1 ch, 768 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 768000bps
    + 4, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 3:
  + index 3
  + duration: 00:03:34
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:34
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
"""


def test_parse_hms():
    assert parse_hms("00:52:36") == 3156
    assert parse_hms("00:00:25") == 25


def test_parse_scan_extracts_titles_chapters_and_audio():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    assert [t.number for t in titles] == [1, 2, 3]

    album = titles[1]
    assert album.length_seconds == 3156
    assert [c.length_seconds for c in album.chapters] == [215, 178]
    assert len(album.audio_tracks) == 4
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].codec == "AC3"
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].channels == 6
    assert album.audio_tracks[2].codec == "DTS"


def test_surround_ac3_track_picks_six_channel_ac3_not_dts():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    album = titles[1]
    track = album.surround_ac3_track()
    assert track is not None
    assert track.index == 2
    assert track.codec == "AC3"
    assert track.channels == 6


def test_surround_ac3_track_none_when_absent():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    single_song = titles[2]
    assert single_song.surround_ac3_track() is None


def test_pick_album_title_prefers_longest_multi_chapter_surround_title():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    chosen = pick_album_title(titles)
    assert chosen.number == 2


def test_track_filenames_uses_names_when_count_matches():
    names = track_filenames(2, ["Hello Sunshine", "Liberty Belle"])
    assert names == ["01 - Hello Sunshine.ac3", "02 - Liberty Belle.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_falls_back_when_count_mismatches():
    names = track_filenames(3, ["Only One Track"])
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3", "track03.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_generic_when_no_names_given():
    names = track_filenames(2, None)
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3"]


def test_sanitize_filename_strips_path_hostile_characters():
    assert sanitize_filename("Sex, War & Robots") == "Sex, War & Robots"
    assert sanitize_filename("Father / Father?") == "Father - Father-"

aiTitle: Extract AC3 surround audio from DVD media files

content.text:
Committed as `afcac4b`.

**What changed:** ffmpeg's raw AC3 muxer turned out to silently drop `-metadata` entirely (confirmed by testing), so tagging now happens as a separate pass with `mutagen`, prepending a proper ID3v2 header after each chapter is extracted. ---
name: project-sfa-extractor
description: Purpose, status, and technical approach of the sfa-extractor DVD-audio ripping tool
metadata:
  type: project
---

`/Users/rod/build/sfa-extractor` is Rod's personal tool for pulling the 5.1 surround AC3 mix off DVD-Video album releases he owns (originally Super Furry Animals discs, but it's generic and has also been run against a Björk disc) and splitting it into one tagged `.ac3` file per track.

As of 2026-07-25, three albums have been extracted successfully: Phantom Power (SFA, 14 tracks), Rings Around the World (SFA, 13 tracks), Post (Björk, 11 tracks). More may follow — ask for the `.dvdmedia` path and a MusicBrainz release ID (MBID) when Rod names a new one.

**Why:** archiving 5.1 mixes from DVD-Audio-era discs he owns before the discs/drives degrade; wants clean per-track files with correct ID3 metadata for his library.

**How to apply:** `uv run extract_ac3.py "<dvd path>" --musicbrainz-release <mbid>` defaults to a dry run (prints the detected title/chapters/track-name plan, writes nothing) — always show Rod that plan and get explicit confirmation before adding `--yes`, even though the tool itself is now proven across three different discs. See [[feedback-dry-run-confirm]].

Key technical findings baked into the script (also documented inline in code, but worth knowing before touching DVD-audio extraction again):
- Homebrew's ffmpeg has no libdvdread/dvdvideo demuxer, and naive `ffmpeg concat:` of a title's multi-part VOB files can produce a **silently duplicated/doubled-length** audio stream on discs where PGC cells reset timestamps mid-title (confirmed on the Phantom Power disc: naive concat gave 6519s instead of the true 3156s). HandBrakeCLI bundles its own libdvdread/libdvdnav and navigates chapters/cells correctly — it's load-bearing, not a convenience.
- ffmpeg's raw `ac3` muxer silently drops `-metadata` — no error, tags just don't land. ID3v2 tags are written as a separate pass with `mutagen` after extraction (ID3v2 is just a prepended header block, so it works fine on a bare elementary stream).
- MusicBrainz's release lookup needs `inc=recordings+artist-credits` — `artist-credit` is NOT included by default even for the release's own top-level artist field; omitting it silently returns `Unknown Artist` rather than erroring.
- Title/chapter auto-detection (longest multi-chapter title with a 6-channel AC3 track) has generalized cleanly across all three discs so far, each with different title numbers and audio track indices — no per-disc hardcoding has been needed.

---
name: feedback-dry-run-confirm
description: Rod wants an explicit confirm step before every real (mutating) run of a repeatable extraction/generation script, even after it's proven
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Even once a script is written, tested, and has already succeeded on prior runs, still show Rod the dry-run/plan output and get explicit go-ahead (AskUserQuestion or equivalent) before the mutating/real run — don't assume "it worked last time" is enough to skip confirmation.

**Why:** confirmed repeatedly in [[project-sfa-extractor]] — for each of three DVD extractions, Rod was shown the dry-run plan and asked "run it for real?" before I passed `--yes`, and never said "just always run it automatically from now on." He held off once ("Not yet") purely to check something first, which validates the value of the pause.

**How to apply:** for any tool in this repo (or similar personal-utility repos) that writes files, spends real time, or hits an external API repeatedly, default to a dry-run mode and ask before the real run each time it's invoked with new input — not just the first time the tool existed.

input.content:
Spent a session ripping 5.1 surround AC3 mixes off old DVD-Audio-style discs (Super Furry Animals x2, Björk's Post) into per-track files. 🎧💿

Biggest gotcha: naive `ffmpeg concat:` of a title's split VOB parts *silently* produced a doubled-length, duplicated audio stream on one disc — no error, just wrong. Turned out the DVD's PGC cells reset timestamps mid-title and ffmpeg's demuxer has zero awareness of DVD chapter/cell structure (no libdvdread in the Homebrew build anyway). Swapped to HandBrakeCLI, which bundles its own libdvdread/libdvdnav, for chapter-accurate extraction — then ffmpeg just strips the throwaway video pass.

Bonus trap: ffmpeg's raw `ac3` muxer swallows `-metadata` with zero complaint. Tags went in via a separate `mutagen` pass instead — ID3v2 is just a prepended header block, so it happily attaches to a bare elementary stream.

Lesson: when a tool silently "succeeds" with corrupted output and no error, don't trust the container format's own duration self-report — verify against an independent source (MusicBrainz track lengths saved me here). 🔍✅

input.technical_insights:
DVD-Video/DVD-Audio hybrid discs (Super Furry Animals Phantom Power/Rings Around the World, Björk Post) can have a "play whole album" title whose multi-part VOB files reset PTS/SCR mid-title at cell boundaries — not just at file-part boundaries. Naive `ffmpeg -i "concat:a.VOB|b.VOB|..."` with `-c:a copy` does NOT reliably reconstruct a clean continuous stream here: ffmpeg's discontinuity-correction heuristic can over-correct and produce a stream at ~2x the true duration with genuinely duplicated audio data (confirmed by file-size math matching the bitrate expectation for the doubled length, not a metadata-only bug). ffmpeg has no libdvdread/dvdvideo demuxer in the standard Homebrew build, so it has no real understanding of DVD chapter/cell/PGC structure — it's just reading bytes.

Fix: HandBrakeCLI bundles its own libdvdread/libdvdnav and correctly navigates PGC/chapter/cell structure regardless of how convoluted the disc's title table is (one disc reported 74 titles for what a user would call one album — that's normal DVD authoring, not corruption). Verified HandBrake's per-chapter extraction against lsdvd's independently-reported chapter lengths and they matched to the millisecond (4107 video frames @ 25fps = exactly the expected chapter duration). Two-step extraction: HandBrakeCLI cuts a chapter-accurate mkv (video must be encoded, even throwaway ultrafast/q51, since HandBrake has no "skip video" mode), then ffmpeg strips video and copies just the AC3 elementary stream out.

Separately: ffmpeg's raw `ac3` muxer silently drops `-metadata`/`-write_id3v2` flags — no warning, no error, tags just don't appear in the output file. Verified by hex-dumping the output (starts with the AC3 sync word 0x0B77, no "ID3" header). Fix was a second pass with `mutagen.id3.ID3()` + `.save()`, which works fine on non-MP3 files since ID3v2 is just a prepended header block, format-agnostic by design.

MusicBrainz `ws/2/release` lookups: `artist-credit` is NOT included by default even though it's a "core" release field — needs explicit `inc=artist-credits` (in addition to `inc=recordings` for track listings) or the artist field is silently empty/missing rather than erroring.
input.user_context:
Rod (British, low-friction collaborator, personal project here distinct from his Splice work) runs a consistent dry-run-then-confirm loop for repeatable/mutating scripts: even after extract_ac3.py was proven correct on the first album, he still wanted the dry-run plan shown and an explicit go-ahead before each subsequent real run (second and third albums) — never asked to skip the confirmation once trust was established. Once when asked "run it for real?" he said "Not yet" with no further explanation and picked back up later without friction; the pause cost nothing and he didn't need to justify it. Take-away: for personal-tool workflows like this, default to showing the plan and asking every time input changes (new disc, new MBID), not just the first time the tool is built.

He's methodical about verifying claims with independent data rather than trusting a single tool's self-report — the MusicBrainz track-length cross-check against lsdvd/HandBrake chapter data was exactly the kind of sanity check that caught the ffmpeg concat corruption early, before it silently shipped wrong output.
input.project_notes: sfa-extractor (/Users/rod/build/sfa-extractor): personal DVD 5.1 AC3 ripper. Despite the name, it's disc-agnostic — proven on 3 different discs (2x Super Furry Animals, 1x Björk) with zero per-disc hardcoding needed. Auto-detection heuristic (longest multi-chapter HandBrake title carrying a 6-channel AC3 track) generalized cleanly even though title numbers and audio track indices differed across all three discs. Stack: HandBrakeCLI (DVD navigation) + ffmpeg (video stripping) + mutagen (ID3v2) + MusicBrainz API (track/artist/album/date metadata), stdlib-only Python otherwise, uv/ruff/pytest per Rod's usual conventions. Output lives in gitignored ./output/, script + tests are committed. Two commits so far: initial extractor, then ID3 tagging addition.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Extract the 5.1 surround AC3 mix from a DVD-Video album release.
3	
4	Uses HandBrakeCLI (which bundles its own DVD chapter/cell navigation) to find
5	the main "play the album" title and cut it into one AC3 file per chapter.
6	Track/artist/album metadata is optionally sourced from a MusicBrainz release
7	and written as ID3v2 tags on each output file.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import argparse
13	import json
14	import re
15	import shutil
16	import subprocess
17	import sys
18	import urllib.request
19	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	from mutagen.id3 import ID3, TALB, TDRC, TIT2, TPE1, TRCK, ID3NoHeaderError
23	
24	MUSICBRAINZ_API = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/{mbid}?inc=recordings+artist-credits&fmt=json"
25	USER_AGENT = "sfa-extractor/0.1 (personal use script)"
26	
27	REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("HandBrakeCLI", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe")
28	
29	
30	class ExtractionError(RuntimeError):
31	    pass
32	
33	
34	@dataclass
35	class Chapter:
36	    number: int
37	    length_seconds: float
38	
39	
40	@dataclass
41	class AudioTrack:
42	    index: int
43	    codec: str
44	    channels: int
45	
46	
47	@dataclass
48	class Title:
49	    number: int
50	    length_seconds: float
51	    chapters: list[Chapter] = field(default_factory=list)
52	    audio_tracks: list[AudioTrack] = field(default_factory=list)
53	
54	    def surround_ac3_track(self) -> AudioTrack | None:
55	        for track in self.audio_tracks:
56	            if track.codec == "AC3" and track.channels == 6:
57	                return track
58	        return None
59	
60	
61	def check_tools() -> None:
62	    missing = [tool for tool in REQUIRED_TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
63	    if missing:
64	        raise ExtractionError(
65	            f"Required tool(s) not found on PATH: {', '.join(missing)}. "
66	            "Install with: brew install handbrake ffmpeg"
67	        )
68	
69	
70	def run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
71	    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
72	    if result.returncode != 0:
73	        raise ExtractionError(f"Command failed ({' '.join(cmd)}):\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}")
74	    return result.stdout + result.stderr
75	
76	
77	def find_video_ts(dvd_path: Path) -> Path:
78	    if dvd_path.name.upper() == "VIDEO_TS":
79	        return dvd_path
80	    candidate = dvd_path / "VIDEO_TS"
81	    if candidate.is_dir():
82	        return candidate
83	    raise ExtractionError(f"No VIDEO_TS folder found under {dvd_path}")
84	
85	
86	def parse_hms(text: str) -> float:
87	    hours, minutes, seconds = text.split(":")
88	    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + int(seconds)
89	
90	
91	TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\+ title (\d+):$")
92	DURATION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ duration: (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
93	CHAPTER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+): duration (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
94	AUDIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+), \S+ \((\w+), (\d+)\.(\d+) ch")
95	
96	
97	def parse_scan(scan_output: str) -> list[Title]:
98	    """Parse HandBrakeCLI's `+ title N:` human-readable scan summary.
99	
100	    Chapter and audio-track lines have distinct, specific shapes ("N: duration
101	    H:M:S" vs "N, Lang (CODEC, C.C ch, ...)"), so no per-line section-tracking
102	    is needed beyond attributing each line to the current title block.
103	    """
104	    titles: list[Title] = []
105	    current: Title | None = None
106	
107	    for line in scan_output.splitlines():
108	        if match := TITLE_RE.match(line):
109	            if current is not None:
110	                titles.append(current)
111	            current = Title(int(match.group(1)), 0.0)
112	            continue
113	        if current is None:
114	            continue
115	        if match := DURATION_RE.match(line):
116	            current.length_seconds = parse_hms(match.group(1))
117	        elif match := CHAPTER_RE.match(line):
118	            current.chapters.append(Chapter(int(match.group(1)), parse_hms(match.group(2))))
119	        elif match := AUDIO_RE.match(line):
120	            channels = int(match.group(3)) + int(match.group(4))
121	            current.audio_tracks.append(AudioTrack(int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), channels))
122	
123	    if current is not None:
124	        titles.append(current)
125	    return titles
126	
127	
128	def scan_disc(dvd_path: Path) -> list[Title]:
129	    output = run(["HandBrakeCLI", "-i", str(dvd_path), "--scan", "-t", "0"])
130	    titles = parse_scan(output)
131	    if not titles:
132	        raise ExtractionError("HandBrakeCLI scan returned no titles")
133	    return titles
134	
135	
136	def pick_album_title(titles: list[Title]) -> Title:
137	    candidates = [t for t in titles if len(t.chapters) > 1 and t.surround_ac3_track() is not None]
138	    if not candidates:
139	        raise ExtractionError("No multi-chapter title with a 5.1 AC3 track found")
140	    return max(candidates, key=lambda t: t.length_seconds)
141	
142	
143	@dataclass
144	class AlbumMetadata:
145	    title: str
146	    artist: str
147	    date: str | None
148	    track_titles: list[str]
149	
150	
151	def _format_artist_credit(artist_credit: list[dict]) -> str:
152	    return "".join(credit["name"] + credit.get("joinphrase", "") for credit in artist_credit)
153	
154	
155	def fetch_musicbrainz_release(mbid: str) -> AlbumMetadata:
156	    url = MUSICBRAINZ_API.format(mbid=mbid)
157	    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
158	    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
159	        data = json.load(response)
160	    medium = data["media"][0]
161	    artist = _format_artist_credit(data.get("artist-credit", [])) or "Unknown Artist"
162	    return AlbumMetadata(
163	        title=data["title"],
164	        artist=artist,
165	        date=data.get("date"),
166	        track_titles=[track["title"] for track in medium["tracks"]],
167	    )
168	
169	
170	def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
171	    return re.sub(r'[/:\\?*"<>|]', "-", name).strip()
172	
173	
174	def track_filenames(count: int, track_titles: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
175	    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) == count:
176	        return [
177	            f"{i:02d} - {sanitize_filename(title)}.ac3"
178	            for i, title in enumerate(track_titles, start=1)
179	        ]
180	    return [f"track{i:02d}.ac3" for i in range(1, count + 1)]
181	
182	
183	def extract_chapter(
184	    dvd_path: Path,
185	    title: Title,
186	    audio_track: AudioTrack,
187	    chapter_number: int,
188	    out_path: Path,
189	    tmp_path: Path,
190	) -> None:
191	    run(
192	        [
193	            "HandBrakeCLI",
194	            "-i",
195	            str(dvd_path),
196	            "-t",
197	            str(title.number),
198	            "--chapters",
199	            f"{chapter_number}-{chapter_number}",
200	            "-a",
201	            str(audio_track.index),
202	            "-E",
203	            "copy:ac3",
204	            "-e",
205	            "x264",
206	            "--encoder-preset",
207	            "ultrafast",
208	            "-q",
209	            "51",
210	            "-o",
211	            str(tmp_path),
212	        ]
213	    )
214	    run(
215	        [
216	            "ffmpeg",
217	            "-y",
218	            "-v",
219	            "error",
220	            "-i",
221	            str(tmp_path),
222	            "-vn",
223	            "-map",
224	            "0:a:0",
225	            "-c:a",
226	            "copy",
227	            "-f",
228	            "ac3",
229	            str(out_path),
230	        ]
231	    )
232	    tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
233	
234	
235	def write_id3_tags(
236	    path: Path,
237	    title: str,
238	    artist: str,
239	    album: str,
240	    track_number: int,
241	    track_total: int,
242	    date: str | None,
243	) -> None:
244	    """Prepend an ID3v2 tag to a raw AC3 file.
245	
246	    Raw AC3 has no native metadata container (ffmpeg's `ac3` muxer silently
247	    drops `-metadata`), but ID3v2 tags are just a header block prepended to
248	    the file, so they attach fine to any file type -- this is the same trick
249	    id3v2-aware players already use for tagging bare AC3/DTS rips.
250	    """
251	    try:
252	        tags = ID3(path)
253	    except ID3NoHeaderError:
254	        tags = ID3()
255	    tags.setall("TIT2", [TIT2(encoding=3, text=title)])
256	    tags.setall("TPE1", [TPE1(encoding=3, text=artist)])
257	    tags.setall("TALB", [TALB(encoding=3, text=album)])
258	    tags.setall("TRCK", [TRCK(encoding=3, text=f"{track_number}/{track_total}")])
259	    if date:
260	        tags.setall("TDRC", [TDRC(encoding=3, text=date)])
261	    tags.save(path, v2_version=3)
262	
263	
264	def extract_album(
265	    dvd_path: Path,
266	    output_dir: Path,
267	    musicbrainz_release: str | None,
268	    title_override: int | None,
269	    confirm: bool,
270	) -> None:
271	    check_tools()
272	    find_video_ts(dvd_path)  # validates the path early
273	
274	    titles = scan_disc(dvd_path)
275	    if title_override is not None:
276	        matches = [t for t in titles if t.number == title_override]
277	        if not matches:
278	            raise ExtractionError(f"Title {title_override} not found on disc")
279	        album_title = matches[0]
280	    else:
281	        album_title = pick_album_title(titles)
282	
283	    audio_track = album_title.surround_ac3_track()
284	    if audio_track is None:
285	        raise ExtractionError(f"Title {album_title.number} has no 5.1 AC3 track")
286	
287	    album_metadata = fetch_musicbrainz_release(musicbrainz_release) if musicbrainz_release else None
288	    if album_metadata is not None and len(album_metadata.track_titles) != len(album_title.chapters):
289	        print(
290	            f"Warning: MusicBrainz release has {len(album_metadata.track_titles)} tracks but "
291	            f"the DVD title has {len(album_title.chapters)} chapters. Falling back to generic "
292	            "naming, no ID3 tags will be written.",
293	            file=sys.stderr,
294	        )
295	        album_metadata = None
296	
297	    track_titles = album_metadata.track_titles if album_metadata is not None else None
298	    filenames = track_filenames(len(album_title.chapters), track_titles)
299	    track_total = len(filenames)
300	
301	    print(
302	        f"Title {album_title.number}: {album_title.length_seconds:.0f}s, "
303	        f"{len(album_title.chapters)} chapters"
304	    )
305	    print(f"Audio track {audio_track.index}: {audio_track.codec} {audio_track.channels}ch")
306	    print(f"ID3 tags: {'yes, from MusicBrainz' if album_metadata is not None else 'no'}")
307	    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
308	        print(f"  {chapter.number:02d}  {chapter.length_seconds:7.1f}s  -> {filename}")
309	
310	    if not confirm:
311	        print("\nDry run only (pass --yes to actually extract). No files written.")
312	        return
313	
314	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
315	    tmp_path = output_dir / ".chapter_tmp.mkv"
316	    for i, (chapter, filename) in enumerate(zip(album_title.chapters, filenames), start=1):
317	        out_path = output_dir / filename
318	        extract_chapter(dvd_path, album_title, audio_track, chapter.number, out_path, tmp_path)
319	        if album_metadata is not None:
320	            write_id3_tags(
321	                out_path,
322	                title=album_metadata.track_titles[i - 1],
323	                artist=album_metadata.artist,
324	                album=album_metadata.title,
325	                track_number=i,
326	                track_total=track_total,
327	                date=album_metadata.date,
328	            )
329	        print(f"Wrote {out_path}")
330	
331	
332	def main() -> None:
333	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
334	    parser.add_argument("dvd_path", type=Path, help="Path to a .dvdmedia bundle or VIDEO_TS folder")
335	    parser.add_argument(
336	        "--output-dir",
337	        type=Path,
338	        default=None,
339	        help="Where to write .ac3 files (default: ./output/<dvd folder name>)",
340	    )
341	    parser.add_argument(
342	        "--musicbrainz-release",
343	        metavar="MBID",
344	        help="MusicBrainz release ID to source track names from",
345	    )
346	    parser.add_argument(
347	        "--title",
348	        type=int,
349	        default=None,
350	        help="Force a specific DVD title number instead of auto-detecting the album title",
351	    )
352	    parser.add_argument(
353	        "--yes",
354	        action="store_true",
355	        help="Actually write files (default is a dry run that just prints the plan)",
356	    )
357	    args = parser.parse_args()
358	
359	    output_dir = args.output_dir or Path("output") / args.dvd_path.stem
360	    try:
361	        extract_album(args.dvd_path, output_dir, args.musicbrainz_release, args.title, args.yes)
362	    except ExtractionError as exc:
363	        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
364	        sys.exit(1)
365	
366	
367	if __name__ == "__main__":
368	    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the 5.1 surround AC3 mix from a DVD-Video album release.

Uses HandBrakeCLI (which bundles its own DVD chapter/cell navigation) to find
the main "play the album" title and cut it into one AC3 file per chapter.
Track/artist/album metadata is optionally sourced from a MusicBrainz release
and written as ID3v2 tags on each output file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

from mutagen.id3 import ID3, TALB, TDRC, TIT2, TPE1, TRCK, ID3NoHeaderError

MUSICBRAINZ_API = "https://musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release/{mbid}?inc=recordings+artist-credits&fmt=json"
USER_AGENT = "sfa-extractor/0.1 (personal use script)"

REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("HandBrakeCLI", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe")


class ExtractionError(RuntimeError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Chapter:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float


@dataclass
class AudioTrack:
    index: int
    codec: str
    channels: int


@dataclass
class Title:
    number: int
    length_seconds: float
    chapters: list[Chapter] = field(default_factory=list)
    audio_tracks: list[AudioTrack] = field(default_factory=list)

    def surround_ac3_track(self) -> AudioTrack | None:
        for track in self.audio_tracks:
            if track.codec == "AC3" and track.channels == 6:
                return track
        return None


def check_tools() -> None:
    missing = [tool for tool in REQUIRED_TOOLS if shutil.which(tool) is None]
    if missing:
        raise ExtractionError(
            f"Required tool(s) not found on PATH: {', '.join(missing)}. "
            "Install with: brew install handbrake ffmpeg"
        )


def run(cmd: list[str]) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Command failed ({' '.join(cmd)}):\n{result.stderr[-2000:]}")
    return result.stdout + result.stderr


def find_video_ts(dvd_path: Path) -> Path:
    if dvd_path.name.upper() == "VIDEO_TS":
        return dvd_path
    candidate = dvd_path / "VIDEO_TS"
    if candidate.is_dir():
        return candidate
    raise ExtractionError(f"No VIDEO_TS folder found under {dvd_path}")


def parse_hms(text: str) -> float:
    hours, minutes, seconds = text.split(":")
    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + int(seconds)


TITLE_RE = re.compile(r"^\+ title (\d+):$")
DURATION_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ duration: (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
CHAPTER_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+): duration (\d+:\d+:\d+)$")
AUDIO_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*\+ (\d+), \S+ \((\w+), (\d+)\.(\d+) ch")


def parse_scan(scan_output: str) -> list[Title]:
    """Parse HandBrakeCLI's `+ title N:` human-readable scan summary.

    Chapter and audio-track lines have distinct, specific shapes ("N: duration
    H:M:S" vs "N, Lang (CODEC, C.C ch, ...)"), so no per-line section-tracking
    is needed beyond attributing each line to the current title block.
    """
    titles: list[Title] = []
    current: Title | None = None

    for line in scan_output.splitlines():
        if match := TITLE_RE.match(line):
            if current is not None:
                titles.append(current)
            current = Title(int(match.group(1)), 0.0)
            continue
        if current is None:
            continue
        if match := DURATION_RE.match(line):
            current.length_seconds = parse_hms(match.group(1))
        elif match := CHAPTER_RE.match(line):
            current.chapters.append(Chapter(int(match.group(1)), parse_hms(match.group(2))))
        elif match := AUDIO_RE.match(line):
            channels = int(match.group(3)) + int(match.group(4))
            current.audio_tracks.append(AudioTrack(int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), channels))

    if current is not None:
        titles.append(current)
    return titles


def scan_disc(dvd_path: Path) -> list[Title]:
    output = run(["HandBrakeCLI", "-i", str(dvd_path), "--scan", "-t", "0"])
    titles = parse_scan(output)
    if not titles:
        raise ExtractionError("HandBrakeCLI scan returned no titles")
    return titles


def pick_album_title(titles: list[Title]) -> Title:
    candidates = [t for t in titles if len(t.chapters) > 1 and t.surround_ac3_track() is not None]
    if not candidates:
        raise ExtractionError("No multi-chapter title with a 5.1 AC3 track found")
    return max(candidates, key=lambda t: t.length_seconds)


@dataclass
class AlbumMetadata:
    title: str
    artist: str
    date: str | None
    track_titles: list[str]


def _format_artist_credit(artist_credit: list[dict]) -> str:
    return "".join(credit["name"] + credit.get("joinphrase", "") for credit in artist_credit)


def fetch_musicbrainz_release(mbid: str) -> AlbumMetadata:
    url = MUSICBRAINZ_API.format(mbid=mbid)
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:
        data = json.load(response)
    medium = data["media"][0]
    artist = _format_artist_credit(data.get("artist-credit", [])) or "Unknown Artist"
    return AlbumMetadata(
        title=data["title"],
        artist=artist,
        date=data.get("date"),
        track_titles=[track["title"] for track in medium["tracks"]],
    )


def sanitize_filename(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r'[/:\\?*"<>|]', "-", name).strip()


def track_filenames(count: int, track_titles: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    if track_titles is not None and len(track_titles) == count:
        return [
            f"{i:02d} - {sanitize_filename(title)}.ac3"
            for i, title in enumerate(track_titles, start=1)
        ]
    return [f"track{i:02d}.ac3" for i in range(1, count + 1)]


def extract_chapter(
    dvd_path: Path,
    title: Title,
    audio_track: AudioTrack,
    chapter_number: int,
    out_path: Path,
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    run(
        [
            "HandBrakeCLI",
            "-i",
            str(dvd_path),
            "-t",
            str(title.number),
            "--chapters",
            f"{chapter_number}-{chapter_number}",
            "-a",
            str(audio_track.index),
            "-E",
            "copy:ac3",
            "-e",
            "x264",
            "--encoder-preset",
            "ultrafast",
            "-q",
            "51",
            "-o",
            str(tmp_path),
        ]
    )
    run(
        [
            "ffmpeg",
            "-y",
            "-v",
            "error",
            "-i",
            str(tmp_path),
            "-vn",
            "-map",
            "0:a:0",
            "-c:a",
            "copy",
            "-f",
            "ac3",
            str(out_path),
        ]
    )
    tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def write_id3_tags(
    path: Path,
    title: str,
    artist: str,
    album: str,
    track_number: int,
    track_total: int,
    date: str | None,
) -> None:
    """Prepend an ID3v2 tag to a raw AC3 file.

    Raw AC3 has no native metadata container (ffmpeg's `ac3` muxer silently
    drops `-metadata`), but ID3v2 tags are just a header block prepended to
    the file, so they attach fine to any file type -- this is the same trick
    id3v2-aware players already use for tagging bare AC3/DTS rips.
    """
    try:
        tags = ID3(path)
    except ID3NoHeaderError:
        tags = ID3()
    tags.setall("TIT2", [TIT2(encoding=3, text=title)])
    tags.setall("TPE1", [TPE1(encoding=3, text=artist)])
    tags.setall("TALB", [TALB(encoding=3, text=album)])
    tags.setall("TRCK", [TRCK(encoding=3, text=f"{track_number}/{track_total}")])
    if date:
        tags.setall("TDRC", [TDRC(encoding=3, text=date)])
    tags.save(path, v2_version=3)


def extract_album(
    dvd_path: Path,
    output_dir: Path,
    musicbrainz_release: str | None,
    title_override: int | None,
    confirm: bool,
) -> None:
    check_tools()
    find_video_ts(dvd_path)  # validates the path early

    titles = scan_disc(dvd_path)
    if title_override is not None:
        matches = [t for t in titles if t.number == title_override]
        if not matches:
            raise ExtractionError(f"Title {title_override} not found on disc")
        album_title = matches[0]
    else:
        album_title = pick_album_title(titles)

    audio_track = album_title.surround_ac3_track()
    if audio_track is None:
        raise ExtractionError(f"Title {album_title.number} has no 5.1 AC3 track")

    album_metadata = fetch_musicbrainz_release(musicbrainz_release) if musicbrainz_release else None
    if album_metadata is not None and len(album_metadata.track_titles) != len(album_title.chapters):
        print(
            f"Warning: MusicBrainz release has {len(album_metadata.track_titles)} tracks but "
            f"the DVD title has {len(album_title.chapters)} chapters. Falling back to generic "
            "naming, no ID3 tags will be written.",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        album_metadata = None

    track_titles = album_metadata.track_titles if album_metadata is not None else None
    filenames = track_filenames(len(album_title.chapters), track_titles)
    track_total = len(filenames)

    print(
        f"Title {album_title.number}: {album_title.length_seconds:.0f}s, "
        f"{len(album_title.chapters)} chapters"
    )
    print(f"Audio track {audio_track.index}: {audio_track.codec} {audio_track.channels}ch")
    print(f"ID3 tags: {'yes, from MusicBrainz' if album_metadata is not None else 'no'}")
    for chapter, filename in zip(album_title.chapters, filenames):
        print(f"  {chapter.number:02d}  {chapter.length_seconds:7.1f}s  -> {filename}")

    if not confirm:
        print("\nDry run only (pass --yes to actually extract). No files written.")
        return

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp_path = output_dir / ".chapter_tmp.mkv"
    for i, (chapter, filename) in enumerate(zip(album_title.chapters, filenames), start=1):
        out_path = output_dir / filename
        extract_chapter(dvd_path, album_title, audio_track, chapter.number, out_path, tmp_path)
        if album_metadata is not None:
            write_id3_tags(
                out_path,
                title=album_metadata.track_titles[i - 1],
                artist=album_metadata.artist,
                album=album_metadata.title,
                track_number=i,
                track_total=track_total,
                date=album_metadata.date,
            )
        print(f"Wrote {out_path}")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("dvd_path", type=Path, help="Path to a .dvdmedia bundle or VIDEO_TS folder")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Where to write .ac3 files (default: ./output/<dvd folder name>)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--musicbrainz-release",
        metavar="MBID",
        help="MusicBrainz release ID to source track names from",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--title",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help="Force a specific DVD title number instead of auto-detecting the album title",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--yes",
        action="store_true",
        help="Actually write files (default is a dry run that just prints the plan)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    output_dir = args.output_dir or Path("output") / args.dvd_path.stem
    try:
        extract_album(args.dvd_path, output_dir, args.musicbrainz_release, args.title, args.yes)
    except ExtractionError as exc:
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

from mutagen.id3 import ID3

from extract_ac3 import (
    _format_artist_credit,
    parse_hms,
    parse_scan,
    pick_album_title,
    sanitize_filename,
    track_filenames,
    write_id3_tags,
)

# Trimmed real HandBrakeCLI `--scan -t 0` output for the Phantom Power DVD:
# title 1 is a short menu/logo clip, title 2 is the full album, title 3 is a
# single-song title with no 5.1 track variety (only used to prove title 2
# still wins on duration).
SCAN_OUTPUT = """
+ title 1:
  + index 1
  + duration: 00:00:25
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:00:25
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 2:
  + index 2
  + duration: 00:52:36
  + size: 720x576, pixel aspect: 64/45, display aspect: 1.78, 25.000 fps
  + autocrop: 0/0/12/174
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:35
    + 2: duration 00:02:58
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
    + 2, English (AC3, 5.1 ch, 448 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 448000bps
    + 3, English (DTS, 5.1 ch, 768 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 768000bps
    + 4, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 192 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 192000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
+ title 3:
  + index 3
  + duration: 00:03:34
  + chapters:
    + 1: duration 00:03:34
  + audio tracks:
    + 1, English (AC3, 2.0 ch, 256 kbps) (iso639-2: eng), 48000Hz, 256000bps
  + subtitle tracks:
"""


def test_parse_hms():
    assert parse_hms("00:52:36") == 3156
    assert parse_hms("00:00:25") == 25


def test_parse_scan_extracts_titles_chapters_and_audio():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    assert [t.number for t in titles] == [1, 2, 3]

    album = titles[1]
    assert album.length_seconds == 3156
    assert [c.length_seconds for c in album.chapters] == [215, 178]
    assert len(album.audio_tracks) == 4
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].codec == "AC3"
    assert album.audio_tracks[1].channels == 6
    assert album.audio_tracks[2].codec == "DTS"


def test_surround_ac3_track_picks_six_channel_ac3_not_dts():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    album = titles[1]
    track = album.surround_ac3_track()
    assert track is not None
    assert track.index == 2
    assert track.codec == "AC3"
    assert track.channels == 6


def test_surround_ac3_track_none_when_absent():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    single_song = titles[2]
    assert single_song.surround_ac3_track() is None


def test_pick_album_title_prefers_longest_multi_chapter_surround_title():
    titles = parse_scan(SCAN_OUTPUT)
    chosen = pick_album_title(titles)
    assert chosen.number == 2


def test_track_filenames_uses_names_when_count_matches():
    names = track_filenames(2, ["Hello Sunshine", "Liberty Belle"])
    assert names == ["01 - Hello Sunshine.ac3", "02 - Liberty Belle.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_falls_back_when_count_mismatches():
    names = track_filenames(3, ["Only One Track"])
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3", "track03.ac3"]


def test_track_filenames_generic_when_no_names_given():
    names = track_filenames(2, None)
    assert names == ["track01.ac3", "track02.ac3"]


def test_sanitize_filename_strips_path_hostile_characters():
    assert sanitize_filename("Sex, War & Robots") == "Sex, War & Robots"
    assert sanitize_filename("Father / Father?") == "Father - Father-"


def test_format_artist_credit_joins_using_musicbrainz_joinphrase():
    credit = [{"name": "Super Furry Animals", "joinphrase": ""}]
    assert _format_artist_credit(credit) == "Super Furry Animals"

    featuring = [
        {"name": "Artist A", "joinphrase": " feat. "},
        {"name": "Artist B", "joinphrase": ""},
    ]
    assert _format_artist_credit(featuring) == "Artist A feat. Artist B"


def test_write_id3_tags_round_trips_on_a_raw_file(tmp_path):
    # ID3v2 is just a header block prepended to the file, so it doesn't
    # matter that this isn't real AC3 audio -- tagging is format-agnostic.
    target = tmp_path / "track.ac3"
    target.write_bytes(b"\x0b\x77" + b"\x00" * 32)

    write_id3_tags(
        target,
        title="Hello Sunshine",
        artist="Super Furry Animals",
        album="Phantom Power",
        track_number=1,
        track_total=14,
        date="2003-07-21",
    )

    tags = ID3(target)
    assert tags["TIT2"].text == ["Hello Sunshine"]
    assert tags["TPE1"].text == ["Super Furry Animals"]
    assert tags["TALB"].text == ["Phantom Power"]
    assert tags["TRCK"].text == ["1/14"]
    assert tags["TDRC"].text[0].text == "2003-07-21"


def test_write_id3_tags_omits_date_when_none(tmp_path):
    target = tmp_path / "track.ac3"
    target.write_bytes(b"\x0b\x77" + b"\x00" * 32)

    write_id3_tags(
        target, title="T", artist="A", album="B", track_number=1, track_total=1, date=None
    )

    tags = ID3(target)
    assert "TDRC" not in tags

117	    """Parse HandBrakeCLI's `+ title N:` human-readable scan summary.
118	
119	    Chapter and audio-track lines have distinct, specific shapes ("N: duration

121	    is needed beyond attributing each line to the current title block.

Follow-up to my earlier DVD-ripping post: extended the extractor to also pull DTS 5.1 tracks when a disc has them, alongside the AC3 mix. 🎛️

Small design choice worth noting — generalized the codec-specific bits (HandBrakeCLI passthrough encoder name, ffmpeg raw-stream muxer name, file extension) into one small `CodecSpec` dataclass rather than branching on codec strings everywhere. Turned out `copy:dts` and the ffmpeg `dts` muxer both just work the same way `copy:ac3`/`ac3` do, so the generalization was nearly free once the AC3 path was solid.

Fun gotcha to close on: `ffprobe`'s quick `format=duration` on a bare `.dts` elementary stream came in ~2% short of the real length. Nearly flagged it as truncated audio. A full decode pass (`ffmpeg -f null -`) showed the actual content was complete and matched the AC3 file exactly — the quick duration is just a bitrate-based estimate, and DTS apparently estimates worse than AC3 does. Second reminder this session that a container/tool's own self-reported metadata isn't always trustworthy — decode and check independently when it matters. 🔍

`/Users/rod/build/sfa-extractor` is Rod's personal tool for pulling the 5.1 surround AC3 mix off DVD-Video album releases he owns (originally Super Furry Animals discs, but it's generic and has also been run against a Björk disc) and splitting it into one tagged `.ac3` file per track.

As of 2026-07-25, three albums have been extracted successfully: Phantom Power (SFA, 14 tracks), Rings Around the World (SFA, 13 tracks), Post (Björk, 11 tracks). More may follow — ask for the `.dvdmedia` path and a MusicBrainz release ID (MBID) when Rod names a new one.

**Why:** archiving 5.1 mixes from DVD-Audio-era discs he owns before the discs/drives degrade; wants clean per-track files with correct ID3 metadata for his library.

**How to apply:** `uv run extract_ac3.py "<dvd path>" --musicbrainz-release <mbid>` defaults to a dry run (prints the detected title/chapters/track-name plan, writes nothing) — always show Rod that plan and get explicit confirmation before adding `--yes`, even though the tool itself is now proven across three different discs. See [[feedback-dry-run-confirm]].

Key technical findings baked into the script (also documented inline in code, but worth knowing before touching DVD-audio extraction again):
- Homebrew's ffmpeg has no libdvdread/dvdvideo demuxer, and naive `ffmpeg concat:` of a title's multi-part VOB files can produce a **silently duplicated/doubled-length** audio stream on discs where PGC cells reset timestamps mid-title (confirmed on the Phantom Power disc: naive concat gave 6519s instead of the true 3156s). HandBrakeCLI bundles its own libdvdread/libdvdnav and navigates chapters/cells correctly — it's load-bearing, not a convenience.
- ffmpeg's raw `ac3` muxer silently drops `-metadata` — no error, tags just don't land. ID3v2 tags are written as a separate pass with `mutagen` after extraction (ID3v2 is just a prepended header block, so it works fine on a bare elementary stream).
- MusicBrainz's release lookup needs `inc=recordings+artist-credits` — `artist-credit` is NOT included by default even for the release's own top-level artist field; omitting it silently returns `Unknown Artist` rather than erroring.
- Title/chapter auto-detection (longest multi-chapter title with a 6-channel AC3 track) has generalized cleanly across all three discs so far, each with different title numbers and audio track indices — no per-disc hardcoding has been needed.
